title: Orchestrate layered build profiles and stabilize language toolchains
creator: Amelia Park
description: Reduce CI build flakiness and latency by introducing composable BuildKit profiles (fast/dev/stable), migrating language SDKs into isolated runtime images, and stabilizing pinned toolchains. This ticket covers discovery, prototype, rollout plan, and metrics instrumentation to validate reduced median build time and lower cache miss rates.
acceptance_criteria: Define and document three BuildKit profile templates: dev-fast, ci-stable, and release-optimized
Create per-language runtime images for Node/Python/Go with deterministic toolchain installs and SBOMs
Implement layered cache hints and cache-priming job such that CI median build time decreases by >= 30% for common changesets
Add observability: per-job cache hit rate, build latency P50/P95, and CI cost per-merge to the CI dashboard
Roll out migration to 20% of repos as canary and demonstrate zero increase in test flakiness during canary window
progress_updates: 2025-11-04: Kickoff meeting with Infra, DX, and Runtime teams. Aligned on goals and metrics. Agreed to use BuildKit advanced features (cache mounts + export/import).
2025-11-18: Completed audit of top 40 slowest repos. Identified common cache-miss patterns: language install, yarn/pip resolution, docker-layer-churn from monorepo Dockerfiles.
2025-12-02: Prototype dev-fast and ci-stable BuildKit profiles in a small demo repo (redwood-sample). Observed P50 improvement ~28% and P95 ~15% on repeated runs.
2026-01-15: Built canonical Node/Python runtime images with pinned toolchain versions, reproducible installs, and SBOMs. Images published to internal registry with TTL 90 days and immutable tags.
2026-02-02: Implemented cache-priming pipeline scheduled nightly for frequently touched base layers (node-modules, pip-wheel-cache). Increased cache hit rate in demo repos from 42% to 71%.
2026-02-20: Security review requested for publishing runtime images (KMS encryption of credentials). Security Q/A completed; minor changes required to image build job.
2026-03-01: Draft rollout plan for canary (20% -> 50% -> 100%) with automatic rollback on flakiness spike or build-time regression. Dashboard panels and alert rules created.

2026-03-10: Started canary on five medium-size services. Early telemetry: median build time -33%, cache hit rate +22 points. Observed one flaky test unrelated to build changes; triage opened ENG-90912.
risks: Pinned toolchains may lag security updates if not on a regular rotation schedule
Cache priming increases cluster egress and storage costs if not bounded by retention policies
Monorepo Dockerfiles with non-deterministic ordering can still cause cache misses until refactored
Canary could expose hidden flakiness in tests that only manifest with faster builds (timing-sensitive tests)
